name: Uyghur Tribunal
convened_by: Established by Sir Geoffrey Nice QC at the June 2020 request of Dolkun Isa, President of the World Uyghur Congress. Members worked pro bono; funding for witness travel, venue hire and some staff came initially from the World Uyghur Congress.
panel: Sir Geoffrey Nice QC (Chair), Nick Vetch (Vice Chair) and seven other members drawn from law, medicine, academia and business.
question: Whether the People's Republic of China committed genocide, crimes against humanity and torture against Uyghur, Kazakh and other Turkic Muslim populations in Xinjiang.
summary: A London people's tribunal that found, beyond reasonable doubt, that China committed genocide against Uyghurs — through measures to prevent births, not mass killing.

sat.text: A third, live-streamed hearing on leaked Xinjiang government papers.
Judgment delivered at Church House, Westminster.

findings: Torture attributable to the PRC: established beyond reasonable doubt.

Crimes against humanity attributable to the PRC, including deportation or forcible transfer, imprisonment, torture, rape and other sexual violence, enforced sterilisation, persecution, enforced disappearance and other inhumane acts: established beyond reasonable doubt.
Genocide: the tribunal was satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the PRC committed genocide by imposing measures to prevent births, intended to destroy a significant part of the Uyghurs in Xinjiang.

Killing: evidence of killings, but not on a scale that could threaten the destruction of the group. Serious harm: established, but the tribunal could not conclude it was intended to destroy the group.
nuance: The genocide finding rests on one of the five acts listed in the Genocide Convention: imposing measures intended to prevent births (Article II(d)). The tribunal noted this may be the first public, evidence-based determination of genocide on that basis alone.

The tribunal said it would, as a whole, prefer not to make such a finding, because it does not match the public understanding of genocide as mass killing. It made the finding anyway because, it said, the Convention's drafters had deliberately kept that act in.
It applied the criminal standard, beyond reasonable doubt, rather than the lower 'clear and convincing' standard used by an earlier independent report.
legal_status: A people's tribunal with no legal force. In its own words, it had no power to enforce the provision of documents or the attendance of witnesses.

responses.text: Announced sanctions on bodies and individuals including the tribunal and its Chair, describing UK sanctions over Xinjiang as based on lies and disinformation.

responses.by: Governments of the US, UK, Japan and the PRC
responses.text: Requests from the tribunal for information were not met, according to the judgment.
